narrative_purpose: Makes Grace's connection-count mistake anatomical: the much larger store of neurons is packed into orderly one-way cerebellar lanes, while the smaller cortex is dominated by recurrent loops, showing why architecture and integration matter more than the number of parts.

On the right, a smaller sheet of cerebral cortex appears as a compact tangle of fibres repeatedly looping back, crossing between distant patches, and returning into the same regions, with several bright junctions linked in closed circuits.
